words.meaning: A thick dark oil found under the ground.

medium.simple_explanation: A thick, dark liquid found deep underground that we use to make fuel and many other products.
medium.funny_explanation: Think of it as Earth's ancient, gooey 'dinosaur juice' that powers your car and makes your plastic toys.

examples.text: Petroleum is extracted from deep wells before it is turned into gasoline.
Without petroleum, your bus would just be a very large, heavy lawn ornament.

words.meaning: Two or more different things put together.
A series of steps to do something.
Many different types of something.
Parts that make up a whole thing.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author uses this term to describe the various individual components or ingredients that make up the complex mixture of petroleum.
hard.simple_explanation: The basic parts or ingredients that combine to form a whole substance.
hard.funny_explanation: Think of them as the 'squad members' of a mixture. You can't have a boy band without the individual singers, and you can't have petroleum without its constituents!

examples.text: Petrol, diesel, and paraffin wax are some of the constituents of petroleum.
The constituents of my favorite sandwich are bread, cheese, and a suspicious amount of pickles.

hard.real_world_analogy: Ingredients in a cake recipe; flour, eggs, and sugar are the constituents of the cake.

words.meaning: Keeping different things apart from each other.

medium.simple_explanation: The process of pulling different parts of a mixture away from each other.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you spend ten minutes picking the onions out of your burger because they aren't invited to the party.

examples.text: Scientists use heat for separating the different liquids found in oil.
Separating my laundry is easy; I just make a 'clean' pile and a 'maybe-clean' pile.

words.meaning: Smaller parts of a large mixture.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Introduced to explain the different groups of liquids collected at different temperatures during the refining of petroleum.
hard.simple_explanation: The different parts or groups separated from a mixture based on their boiling points.
hard.funny_explanation: In the world of oil, fractions aren't just scary math homework; they are the different 'slices' of the giant petroleum pie that get separated so they can do their own jobs.

examples.text: The various fractions of petroleum are separated in a tall tower called a fractionating column.
When we split the pizza, the 'pineapple-hater' fraction moved to the other side of the room.

hard.real_world_analogy: Sorting a big bag of mixed candy into groups of chocolates, gummies, and lollipops.

words.meaning: The process of making a substance pure.

medium.simple_explanation: The industrial process of cleaning a raw material and breaking it down into useful parts.
medium.funny_explanation: It's like taking a muddy potato and turning it into clean, crispy french fries.

examples.text: Refining oil allows us to get helpful things like jet fuel and wax.
I am currently refining my dance moves, which mostly involves trying not to trip over my own feet.

words.meaning: A factory where crude oil is cleaned.

medium.simple_explanation: A large factory where raw materials like crude oil are processed and turned into products.
medium.funny_explanation: A giant industrial kitchen where the 'chef' cooks up gasoline, plastic, and asphalt instead of soup.

examples.text: The refinery near the coast processes thousands of barrels of oil every day.
The refinery is so big it looks like a playground built for giant robots.

words.meaning: Different types of materials or matter.

medium.simple_explanation: Different types of matter or materials that have specific properties.
medium.funny_explanation: Basically just a fancy science word for 'stuff'—whether it's slime, gold, or pizza sauce.

examples.text: Crude oil contains many different substances that must be sorted out.
There are some very mysterious green substances growing in the back of my school locker.

words.meaning: Something found in nature, not man-made.
A substance like air that flows freely.
Chemicals made from petroleum or natural gas.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The book introduces this to show the massive industrial importance of petroleum in making everyday chemicals.
hard.simple_explanation: Chemical substances derived from petroleum or natural gas.
hard.funny_explanation: These are the 'superhero' chemicals born from oily parents. They transform from gooey black sludge into everything from your toothbrush to your bright t-shirt!

examples.text: Petrochemicals are used to manufacture a wide range of useful substances like plastics and fibers.
I told my mom my plastic toy was basically a pet, because it's made from petrochemicals!

hard.real_world_analogy: Like using LEGO bricks to build totally different things; petroleum is the brick, and petrochemicals are the cool things you build with them.

words.meaning: Soap-like substances used for cleaning.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Mentioned as one of the many commercial products made using petrochemicals.
hard.simple_explanation: Powerful cleaning agents that can remove dirt and grease even in hard water.
hard.funny_explanation: Detergents are like tiny soldiers with magnets that grab onto grease and drag it away from your clothes while you're not looking.

examples.text: Many modern detergents are synthesized from petroleum products.
If it weren't for detergents, I'd still be wearing the chocolate sauce from last year's birthday party.

hard.real_world_analogy: A bulldozer for dirt; it doesn't just ask the dirt to leave, it forces it out.

words.meaning: Thin threads used to make cloth.

medium.simple_explanation: Thin, thread-like strands that can be spun into cloth or rope.
medium.funny_explanation: Tiny microscopic hairs that team up to become the sweater you're wearing right now.

examples.text: Synthetic fibres are often made from chemicals found in oil.
My cat leaves so many fibres on the couch that the sofa is basically 40% feline now.

words.meaning: A strong man-made cloth material.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Listed as a synthetic fiber made from petrochemicals to illustrate petroleum's role in the textile industry.
hard.simple_explanation: A strong, wrinkle-resistant synthetic fabric made from plastic-like chemicals.
hard.funny_explanation: It's basically wearable plastic! Polyester is the reason your sports jersey doesn't turn into a crumpled mess even if you leave it at the bottom of your gym bag for a week.

examples.text: Polyester is often blended with cotton to make durable clothing.
My polyester shirt is so shiny and smooth that even spilled juice just slides right off like a water slide.

hard.real_world_analogy: A spider's web made of plastic; it's thin, light, but very hard to break.

words.meaning: A strong, thin man-made material.

medium.simple_explanation: A strong, man-made material used for making clothes, ropes, and brushes.
medium.funny_explanation: The material responsible for that 'swish-swish' sound your track pants make when you run.

examples.text: The bristles on your toothbrush are usually made of nylon.
If humans lived in the ocean, we'd probably wear nylon suits to stay fast and slippery.

words.meaning: A man-made fibre that feels like wool.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe another type of synthetic fiber that resembles wool, showing the diversity of petroleum products.
hard.simple_explanation: A synthetic fiber that is soft, warm, and feels like wool.
hard.funny_explanation: Acrylic is the 'imposter wool.' It looks like it came from a fluffy sheep, but it actually came from a science lab!

examples.text: Acrylic blankets are popular because they are lightweight and provide warmth.
My sweater is 100% acrylic, which means no sheep were bothered, but I'm still as warm as a toasted muffin.

hard.real_world_analogy: Artificial grass; it looks and feels like the real thing but is actually made of chemicals.

words.meaning: A common type of plastic material.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Mentioned as a very common plastic produced from petroleum, familiar to students in daily life.
hard.simple_explanation: The most common type of plastic, used mainly for packaging and bags.
hard.funny_explanation: The world's most famous plastic! It’s the 'crinkly' stuff that makes up your grocery bags and sandwich wraps.

examples.text: Polythene bags are widely used but can be harmful to the environment if not recycled.
I tried to count how many polythene bags we had under the sink, but I lost count at a million.

hard.real_world_analogy: A thin skin for objects; it wraps them up and keeps them safe from water.

words.meaning: Materials that can be shaped into objects.

medium.simple_explanation: Lightweight, durable materials that can be molded into almost any shape.
medium.funny_explanation: The amazing stuff that can be a soft soda bottle one day and a hard Lego brick the next.

examples.text: Many plastics are manufactured using ingredients from petroleum.
The world is so full of plastics that even the toy fish are made of it.

words.meaning: A very light gas found in nature.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: The author explains that hydrogen gas obtained from natural gas is used to produce fertilizers like urea.
hard.simple_explanation: A colorless, odorless, highly flammable gas; the lightest chemical element.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'baby' of the periodic table! It’s the lightest element and loves to bond with everyone. It's so light that if you had a balloon of it, it would try to fly to the moon.

examples.text: Hydrogen gas is used in the manufacture of fertilizers to help crops grow.
If humans could breathe hydrogen and talk, we'd probably sound like squeaky squirrels!

hard.real_world_analogy: The fuel for stars; the Sun is basically a giant ball of hydrogen having a very loud party.

words.meaning: Substances added to soil to help plants.

medium.simple_explanation: Chemicals or natural substances added to soil to help plants grow big and healthy.
medium.funny_explanation: Vitamins for plants that often smell like a farm's bathroom but make tomatoes huge.

examples.text: Farmers use fertilizers to make sure they grow enough food for everyone.
I tried giving my plastic plant some fertilizers, but it still refused to grow.

words.meaning: Related to buying and selling for profit.

medium.simple_explanation: Relating to the buying and selling of goods to make a profit.
medium.funny_explanation: Anything done for the 'big bucks'—like a lemonade stand that actually makes money.

examples.text: Petroleum has great commercial value because it is used in so many industries.
My dog has no commercial skills; he keeps trying to buy treats with belly rubs.

words.meaning: The state of being very useful.
A very valuable yellow metal.
Fuel used for cars and light vehicles.
Fuel used for heavy vehicles like trucks.
Fuel used for lamps and stoves.

medium.simple_explanation: A type of fuel oil used in lamps and jet engines.
medium.funny_explanation: The liquid that helps planes fly high and keeps old-fashioned lanterns glowing.

examples.text: Before electricity was common, people burned kerosene for light.
You wouldn't want to mistake kerosene for lemonade; your stomach is not a jet engine.

words.meaning: Making parts move smoothly by using oil.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Introduced in the context of 'lubricating oil,' one of the key fractions of petroleum used for machinery.
hard.simple_explanation: Applying a substance to reduce friction between moving surfaces.
hard.funny_explanation: Imagine trying to slide down a slide made of sandpaper—ouch! Lubricating is like putting butter on that slide so you zoom down at light speed.

examples.text: Lubricating oil is essential for keeping car engines running smoothly.
I tried lubricating the squeaky door hinge with leftover pizza grease. It worked, but now the house smells like pepperoni.

hard.real_world_analogy: Oil on a squeaky bicycle chain; it stops the 'screaming' and makes pedaling easy.

words.meaning: A type of wax used for candles.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Describes a specific wax obtained from petroleum used in candles and medical ointments.
hard.simple_explanation: A white, colorless solid wax made from petroleum.
hard.funny_explanation: It's the stuff that makes candles melt and ointments feel slippery on your skin. It's like the quiet, waxy cousin of petrol.

examples.text: Paraffin wax is used to make candles, vaseline, and shoe polish.
My birthday candles are made of paraffin, which is technically 'old dinosaur juice' if you think about it.

hard.real_world_analogy: A crayon's texture; that smooth, slightly greasy feeling is very similar to paraffin.

words.meaning: A solid substance used to make candles.
A black substance used to make roads.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Identified as the petroleum product that has replaced coal tar for surfacing roads.
hard.simple_explanation: A thick, black, sticky form of petroleum used for road surfacing and roofing.
hard.funny_explanation: The 'road glue.' It’s the thick, dark sludge that smells like a construction site and holds the stones together so you don't drive on dirt.

examples.text: Bitumen is preferred over coal tar for making long-lasting road surfaces.
Don't step on fresh bitumen with your new sneakers, or you'll become part of the road forever!

hard.real_world_analogy: Super-thick molasses or honey, but black and used for building things instead of eating.

words.meaning: Something that flows like water.
Having very little light or color.
Feeling like or covered in oil.
Not nice or not enjoyable.

medium.simple_explanation: Something that is not nice, enjoyable, or comfortable.
medium.funny_explanation: The exact feeling of stepping in a cold puddle while wearing only socks.

examples.text: Crude oil has an unpleasant odor that is very strong.
The smell of my brother's gym bag is truly unpleasant.

words.meaning: A strong smell, usually a bad one.

hard.why_it_is_given_in_book: Used to describe the characteristic (and often unpleasant) smell of petroleum and its constituents.
hard.simple_explanation: A distinctive smell, especially an unpleasant one.
hard.funny_explanation: A fancy word for 'stink.' While a perfume has a fragrance, a wet dog or a petrol pump has an odour.

examples.text: Petroleum has a very strong and unpleasant odour.
My brother's gym socks have an odour that could probably be classified as a chemical weapon.

hard.real_world_analogy: An invisible cloud of information that tells your nose exactly what's nearby.

words.meaning: Something that helps to do a task.
To get something from a source.

medium.simple_explanation: To get or acquire something, especially through effort or a specific process.
medium.funny_explanation: Like when you finally 'obtain' the high score after playing the same level for three hours.

examples.text: Useful chemicals are obtained from petroleum during refining.
I have obtained the secret password to the Wi-Fi; I am now unstoppable.

words.meaning: To make something in a factory.

medium.simple_explanation: To make something on a large scale using machinery in a factory.
medium.funny_explanation: A fancy word for 'making stuff' with giant robots and conveyor belts.

examples.text: The company uses oil to manufacture plastic containers.
I wish I could manufacture 100% correct answers during my math test.

words.meaning: A chemical used as a plant fertilizer.

medium.simple_explanation: A chemical compound used in fertilizers to provide nitrogen for plants.
medium.funny_explanation: It's a chemical found in pee, but scientists make it in labs to help corn grow big and tall.

examples.text: Urea is an important ingredient in many agricultural fertilizers.
The plants were so happy with the urea that they practically threw a garden party.

words.meaning: The top layer of something.
One thickness of a material on another.
Tiny grains of crushed rock.
Sticky earth used for making pots.
Material burned to produce energy.
Something that weighs a lot.
Something that does not weigh much.
A hard path for cars to travel.
Colored liquid used to cover surfaces.
A clear liquid we drink to live.
Very big in size or amount.
Information arranged in rows and columns.
Letting someone see or understand something.
Ways in which something can be used.
